task: Generate an independent asymmetric algorithm figure pairing observed paths with a compact endpoint-change summary.
title: Objective path and displayed-window endpoint change
objective: Separate path shape from the arithmetic of the first and last observed values so neither is used as a proxy for the other.
core_conclusion: Within the displayed illustrative trajectories, all three methods end below their displayed starting values and Proposed ends at the lowest displayed objective; the right panel reports only the corresponding displayed-window changes.
claim: Within the displayed illustrative trajectories, all three methods end below their displayed starting values and Proposed ends at the lowest displayed objective; no speed, stability, or general superiority claim is made.
audience: Readers of a mathematical modelling or algorithm research paper

layout.label: a
layout.content: Current objective paths over ten displayed iterations with direct endpoint labels.

layout.label: b
layout.content: First-to-last displayed objective change using open starts, filled ends, and signed net changes.

evidence_panels.question: What paths are directly observed over the displayed iteration window?
How far apart are the first and last displayed objective values?

encoding.endpoint_change: open start to filled end connected by a color-coded segment

uncertainty.reason: One deterministic trajectory per algorithm and no uncertainty estimate are supplied.

review_risks: The endpoint summary is arithmetic within the displayed window, not a convergence-speed metric.
The practice label Proposed must not be interpreted as validated superiority.
The asymmetric layout must remain legible at double-column width and be reported as a stress test at single-column width.
scientific_unknowns: No replicate runs or seeds are available.
No stopping criterion or threshold is supplied.
The input does not establish performance outside ten displayed iterations.
user_reference_note: The supplied journal reference was used for visual methods only; no reference data or claims were reused.
